findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple incidents of employees switching tasks without washing hands. CORRECTED- inspector discussed times to wash hands with the person in charge (PIC). Ensure all employees frequently review required times to wash hands, which includes but is not limited to: after cleaning, after touching personal items, when switching between handling raw and ready to eat food items, etc.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the soap dispenser in the restroom nearest the back door to not be dispensing. CORRECTED, the PIC removed and cleaned the dispenser, to be placed at the sink basin for patrons to dispense themselves. Discussed purchasing a pump soap until the current dispenser is repaired or replaced with the PIC. Ensure all sinks designated for hand washing always have warm running water, paper towels, and soap for proper hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.

findings.citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

findings.comment:
All foods in the 2 door cooler were observed from 49F to 52F (probed). Foods included (but not limited to) pastrami, roast beef, turkey, ham, sliced cheeses, soups, shell eggs, and mayonnaise. findings.comment:

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC at time of inspection still working on food manager course and plans for test for certification in the near future. Ensure proof of food manager certification is available on-site by next routine inspection. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Poblano and cheese soup was observed with surface and internal temperatures at 121F and 125F respectively. Mac-n-cheese and broccoli cheddar soup in the same food warmer had internal temperatures at 149F and 157F. Poblano soup was at the front of the warmer, and it would appear lack of water in the front of the holding compartment caused the temperature of soup to drop slightly. Water was added, and the food warmer was adjusted to highest setting to quickly reheat soup to 165F. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, cross contamination, reheating, sanitization, and date marking. Food thermometer was observed well out of range to allow for proper monitoring of food temperatures. PIC at the time of inspection did not have a food manager certification but is in the process of completing certification.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC at time of inspection had a food handler certification but has not yet completed food manager certification. Store manager with certification was not present. Ensure enough staff have a food manager certification to ensure a person with certification is on-site during all hours of operation to over see prep/service. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC went between tasks without washing hands. Orders were prepared and cashed out prior to putting on gloves to prepare another order. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed. Even if facility is short staffed, handwashing after working the register needs to be a priority before doing any tasks related to food prep/handling, especially before putting on gloves to prepare orders.   
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the kitchen, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and handle of paper towel dispenser was touched to dispense paper towels after hand washing occurred. Proper technique was discussed with staff. Proper handwashing technique poster is located at the handwashing sink for reference.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Mold buildup was observed in the ice machine bin on the baffle and on the ceiling behind the baffle. Mold was also observed in the ice machine under and around the ice maker. Staff were advised of the issue. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing in the ice machine and inside the bin as needed to eliminate mold. 
2. Nozzle of freestyle machine had chunky buildup on it. Ensure freestyle machine nozzle is cleaned and sanitized daily to eliminate buildup.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Flats of raw shell eggs were observed in the 2 door cooler above and next to soup and deli meats. Ensure proper storage of raw shell eggs in the bottom of the cooler below and separate from ready to eat foods regardless of how eggs are packaged/wrapped. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly prepared bleach solution in sani-bucket was observed at 100ppm. Bleach used at facility requires a concentration of 200ppm per manufacturer’s label directions. More bleach was added to provide solution at 200ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration of solutions, and maintain bleach solutions at proper concentration.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Backup portions of potato soup and meatballs had internal temperatures of 120F and 96F-108F respectively. PIC just moved the products to a warmer that was holding tomato soup at 140F. Warmer previously in use was said to be new and may not be working properly but was turned on to heat products during morning prep. PIC noted they were busy and short staffed today and thus didn’t have time to check temperatures prior to service. It would appear the soup and meatballs may have never reached a minimum temperature of 135F and were discarded. 
Ready-to-eat TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Vegetarian products of chicken, meatballs, pepperoni, and ham all had date marks of prep for 10/24 and use by date of 10/30. Another portion of vegetarian ham had a date mark of prep for 10/21 and use by date of 10/27. PIC noted the meatballs were prepared fresh on Monday and had a prep date of 10/30. Meatballs were properly labeled and kept for use. All other products were discarded during inspection.  
2. Hummus in the bottom of the prep cooler was without a date mark. Container was about a quarter full and was discarded during inspection. 
Ensure proper date marking and that all foods are served or discarded by the use by date.
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) Ice scoop was stored in the bin of the ice machine with handle down in the ice. Portion of ice in contact with the handle was discarded, and scoop was relocated to ice bucket for storage. Ensure handle of scoop is extended up and not in direct contact with ice if stored in the ice bin. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in ¶¶ (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Portions of vegetarian turkey, roast beef, ham, turkey, and tomatoes in the bottom of the sandwich prep cooler were observed with dates marks showing the last day of use was 2/7. Additional pans of in-use deli meats and tomatoes were also observed with use by dates of 2/7 in the top of the prep cooler. All foods prepared foods with use by dates of 2/7 were discarded during inspection. A few products had a use by date of 2/8 and were immediately put in the cooler to be used or discarded by the end of operations today.
2. Hummus in the bottom of the prep cooler was without a date mark. Manager noted the product was opened Wednesday of last week. Hummus was to be used or discarded by the end of operations today. 
Ensure proper date marking and that all foods are served or discarded by the use by date.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Box of napkins was observed on the floor near the kitchen handwashing sink, which had a leak at the plumbing beneath the basin. Napkins were delivered ~1 week ago. Soda flats were placed under the box to allow for proper storage. 
Single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:

A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employees working at the time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Employee health policy was discussed, and additional copies of the reporting agreement were provided. Owner and employees signed copies of the reporting agreement during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 In the first half hour inspector was on-site the employees did not wash their hands once. Employees went between tasks and were observed working the cash register, handling a broom and dust pan, as well as exiting and re-entering the kitchen without washing hands. Employees were observed putting on gloves without handwashing as well. Lengthy discussion of when to wash hands occurred. Both employees working the front food service area were observed washing hands properly and as needed for the remainder of inspection.  
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the kitchen, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Concentration of bleach solutions were at 100ppm at the 3 part sink and back sani-bucket. All bleach solutions were remade and observed at 200ppm per label directions of product used at the facility. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration of solutions, and maintain bleach solutions at proper concentration.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was reading around 100F at ambient temperature. Ice water method was used to calibrate the thermometer to 32F during inspection. Ensure the food thermometer is checked, calibrated, and used daily to verify proper temperatures.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen certification was not available for owner. Food allergen awareness certification needs to be completed by all CFMs. 
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed drinking from a personal beverage and touching the straw up near their mouth prior to returning to the 3 part sink to handle clean dishes. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks and washed hands prior to continuing with ware washing. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier and prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Handwashing signage with proper handwashing technique is posted on the paper towel dispenser. Employee was advised on proper handwashing technique.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Chunky mold buildup was observed in the ice machine on surfaces under, in front of, and around the ice tray, as well as on the ceiling behind the baffle. Condensation was observed dripping from the buildup behind the baffle down into the ice bin. Some mold buildup was also observed along the bottom edge of the baffle. PIC emptied the ice machine. All parts that could be removed were washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the 3 part sink. Other surfaces were cleaned and sanitized in place. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency that does not allow for accumulation of mold.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11 Mold buildup was observed on the ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle and on the lower surfaces of the baffle. Cleaning and maintenance of ice machine were discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

4-501.114 Concentration of bleach solutions were at 100ppm at the 3 part sink and in the front counter sani-bucket. Product used to make solutions requires a concentration of 200ppm. All solutions were discarded and fresh solutions prepared at 200ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration of solutions, and maintain bleach solutions at 200ppm per label directions.
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Amount of solution in the sanitize compartment at the 3 part sink was not adequate for proper submersion of baking sheets. The sink was only about a fourth way full with solution and went less than half way up the baking sheets. Even when flipped to sanitize the other end, the middle part of the baking sheets would have no contact time. New solution was provided to allow for proper submersion for baking sheets and adequate contact with sanitizer. 
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 (in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions). Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 10 seconds for chlorine chemical sanitizing solutions.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle with a faint label indicating it contained glass cleaner was observed to have a strong bleach solution and/or a chemical with a bleach component. The solution was clear unlike another bottle of glass cleaner that had blue liquid in it, and inspector's test strip was bleached out by the solution. Liquid was discarded in the mopsink during inspection.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution, etc.) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.
NOTE: If a bleach solution is prepared in a spray bottle, ensure test strips are used to verify concentration is no stronger than 200ppm as required by product available for use.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice bucket and scoop inside were observed on top of the ice machine located under a fan that was blowing down. The fan cover had some dust buildup, and a small piece of debris was observed in the bottom of the bucket. The scoop and ice bucket were set aside to be cleaned and sanitized. Owner also turned the fan on to suction air up into the ceiling as intended rather than blow down on top of the ice machine. Owner was advised to consider a different storage location for the bucket and scoop since the fan is in the ceiling at a spot where a tile has been removed to allow for positioning.  
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.citation_text:

findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solutions in sani-buckets had concentrations of 0ppm and 10ppm chlorine. Solutions were remade and then observed at 100ppm. Label directions for product in use requires a concentration of 200ppm. Solutions remade by owner and verified at 200ppm with test strips. Employee working with owner was advised on proper concentration for product in use
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Meatballs, jerk chicken soup, and potato soup had surface and internal temperatures ranging from 120F-130F. Meatballs and soups were in the right warmer. All products in the left warmer were at 160F/above. Right warmer was adjusted to a higher setting to reheat foods to 165F. Within ~45 minutes foods were above 150F. Staff were advised to stir products and verify proper reheat to 165F prior to serving. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Cheese slices in the top holding area of the prep cooler were observed with surface temperatures above 50F and internal temperatures of 48F and 54F. Cheeses were placed in the cooler at ~1230pm. Owner was advised cheeses could be used or discarded by 630pm as long as they didn't get above 70F. If they warmed above 70F the cheeses need to be discarded by 430pm based on information provided. Cheese was to be used or discarded accordingly based on temperature of product.
Also, surface temperatures of foods were in the high forty degree and low fifty degree farenheit range due to the way foods were stocked. Owner was advised to be careful with overstocking, and products were to be re-portioned so foods were not stocked above ill lines in pans to help maintain colder temperatures. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach currently in use for sanitizing did not have proper labeling. Bleach in question was likely purchased when facility needed to buy some in a pinch. Options for locations to purchase bleach last minute were discussed. Owner was advised to make sure the staff know the label requirements (EPA registration number; instructions for use with food contact surfaces; and concentration listed in ppm for sanitizing food contact surfaces). Proper bleach was available in the storage room and made available for use. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).
